youtube_title: Le Griffon, 1679: the first sailing ship on the upper Great Lakes vanished on its first voyage
body: The first sailing ship on the upper Great Lakes vanished on its first voyage. The French explorer La Salle had the Griffon built in 1679 on the Niagara River, above the falls. That September it reached Green Bay, and La Salle loaded it with furs. On September 18, 1679, he sent it back with a crew of six, and it was never heard from again. That November, La Salle built a fort at the mouth of the St. Joseph River, in today's St. Joseph, Michigan; a state marker there says he awaited his ship, and it did not come. A storm? A mutiny? No one knows. Wreck claims keep coming, and none has been confirmed.
